arguments.title: Field Service Dispatch API Specification
arguments.summary: Design a self-consistent API specification (entities + operations, no implementation) for a field-service dispatch domain: 5 entities and 8 capabilities, built in 6 sequential cards over the single shared spec/api.json file, ending with a completeness flip verified by two real test runs.
arguments.spec:
# Field Service Dispatch API -- specification consistency rules

Deliverable: spec/api.json, an entities+operations specification (no server, no handlers, no schema migrations).
Five domain nouns from input/brief.md must each become one entity: Site, WorkOrder, Appointment, Part, Technician,
spelled exactly as the brief spells them. Eight capabilities (CAP-01..CAP-08) must each be served by at least one
operation.

An entity is {name, identity, fields}. name is PascalCase, unique across the specification. fields is a non-empty
array of {name, type}; field names are camelCase and unique within the entity. identity names one of that entity's
own fields -- an entity you cannot address is not an entity.

An operation is {name, capability, input, output, errors}. name is camelCase, unique across the specification.
capability is one of the brief's CAP-NN ids. input is an array of {name, type}, possibly empty, names unique.
output is a type or "void". errors is a non-empty array of {code, when}: code is SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, unique
within the operation; when is at least twelve characters naming the real condition that produces it, not the code
restated -- every operation in this domain has at least one way to fail, and the brief's closing section is a
checklist of real weekly failures to map onto operations as you go, not a sweep to do afterwards.

Types are the primitives string, integer, decimal, boolean, timestamp, id; any entity this specification defines;
or T[] for an array of any of those. Every type you mention must resolve to a primitive or to an entity you
defined in the same edit -- no dangling references, checked on every save, not only at the end.

Set complete to true only once every domain noun has an entity and every capability is served by an operation --
that is the last card's job alone.

input/**, everything under test/, and scripts/run-tests.mjs are frozen evidence (content-digest checked by
npm test) and must never be edited. The sandbox is offline: never add a dependency.
arguments.plan:
# Plan

Sequential chain over the single shared file spec/api.json (every card writes it, so cards run in strict order,
never in parallel, to avoid a merge race on one file):

1. define-core-entities -- model Site, WorkOrder, Appointment, Part, Technician with real fields and identities.
2. record-site-workorder-operations -- CAP-01 (register a site, keep access notes current), CAP-02 (raise a work
   order with required skills).
3. record-appointment-operations -- CAP-03 (schedule an appointment for a qualified technician), CAP-04 (move or
   cancel an appointment).
4. record-parts-closure-operations -- CAP-05 (reserve parts from van stock), CAP-06 (close a work order recording
   consumed parts).
5. record-query-operations -- CAP-07 (list a technician's day), CAP-08 (find work orders by site and status).
6. finalize-completeness -- flip complete to true once all 5 entities and 8 capabilities are present, verified by
   two real npm test runs (before and after the flip).

Each operations card maps at least one of the brief's named weekly failures onto its own operations' error cases,
so error handling is written with the operation rather than swept in at the end.

tasks.title: Define core domain entities
tasks.prompt: Define the specification's foundational entities in spec/api.json's `entities` array: Site, WorkOrder, Appointment, Part, and Technician, spelled exactly as the brief's domain-noun glossary spells them. Each entity needs a PascalCase `name`, a non-empty `fields` array of `{name, type}` (camelCase names, unique within the entity, types resolving to a primitive or another entity your card defines), and an `identity` field name that is actually one of the entity's own fields. Model what each noun needs to do its job: Site needs an address, a contact, and access notes that go stale and must be kept current (CAP-01); WorkOrder needs a status that moves from raised to closed and the skills the job needs (CAP-02, and the skill-matching CAP-03 depends on); Appointment needs the technician, work order, site and time window it promises (CAP-03, CAP-04); Part needs a reserved quantity and a consumed quantity that can diverge -- 'the gap between reserved and consumed is where the money leaks' (CAP-05, CAP-06); Technician needs a home depot, a skill set and a working day (CAP-03, CAP-07). Do not add any operation in this card -- that is every later card's job. Run npm test after every entity you add; each is checked immediately and strictly, so build them one at a time if the suite complains rather than writing all five before testing. Do not set complete to true.

CAP-02 is raising a work order against a site with the skills the job needs; consider what happens when the cited site does not exist. Every operation needs a camelCase `name`, an `input` array (possibly empty, unique names), an `output` (a type or "void"), and a non-empty `errors` array of {code (SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE), when (at least 12 characters naming the real condition, not the code restated)}.
